title: Measurement-induced dynamics and emergent symmetries of particles moving in a one-dimensional lattice
abstract: Continuous measurements simultaneously reveal and modify the dynamics of a quantum system. In this work we consider the tunneling motion of particles between the sites of a one-dimensional lattice. We investigate how weak continuous probing of the occupation of a single lattice site induces entanglement and selects definite values for system properties such as wave function parity and permutation symmetry. Our simulations show how continuous measurement can steer systems of two and three particles, with no prior permutation symmetry, into stable bosonic, fermionic and parastatistical symmetry sectors.
summary: This paper explores how continuous measurement of a single site in a 1D lattice can fundamentally alter the quantum state of multiple particles. By analyzing the dynamics using stochastic master equations, the authors demonstrate that the system is forced into distinct, stable symmetry sectors—bosonic, fermionic, and a novel immanonic type. This highlights measurement's power to select specific symmetries in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how continuous quantum measurements can induce entanglement and select definite values for fundamental system properties, such as wave function parity and permutation symmetry, in interacting particles.
main_result: Weak continuous probing of a lattice site can steer multi-particle quantum systems into stable symmetry sectors corresponding to bosonic, fermionic, or novel immanonic symmetries.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using the Stochastic Schrödinger Equation (SSE) and Stochastic Master Equation (SME) formalism, extending the Ehrenfest theorem to account for measurement back-action.
model_or_system: The system models tunneling motion of particles on a one-dimensional lattice, analyzed using tight-binding Hamiltonians and incorporating permutation operators for multi-particle states.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy (von Neumann), expectation values of symmetry projection operators ($\langle \hat{P}_{	ext{bos}} angle$, $\langle \hat{P}_{	ext{ferm}} angle$, $\langle \hat{P}(2,1) angle$), and the largest eigenvalue ($\lambda_{\max}$) of the reduced density matrix.
important_parameters: The probing strength (weak continuous probing), the number of particles (two or three), and the lattice hopping parameter ($J$).
main_assumptions: The symmetry classification applies only to the subsector of the Hilbert space accessed by the continuous measurements, not the entire space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the probing scheme for one particle, showing parity selection; and for two/three particles, they show the evolution of symmetry projectors and occupation numbers for different symmetry sectors.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from single-particle parity selection to two-particle symmetry selection (bosonic/fermionic), and finally extends the analysis to three particles to identify and confirm the existence of a third symmetry class, the (2,1)-immanon symmetry.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics under continuous monitoring, a core topic in quantum optics and AMO physics, showing how measurement acts as a non-unitary selection mechanism for quantum states.
